messages.author: 3218795d83a2584e
messages.subject: adjusted p-value calculation in msstats
parts:
Hi,

I am seeking an explanation for the observation I have made while analyzing my dataset in MSstats. It happened that the proteomic core I work with have initially sent me a dataset when the run for one of my bioreplicates has been missing, and then subsequently sent another dataset where all the runs were present. I have analyzed both datasets separately. What I have noticed is that for some quantified proteins I have exactly the same estimation of log2FC and p-value for both datasets, but the adjusted p-value is different. Interestingly, it occurs in the comparison that is not relevant for this added one run since it does not belong to the conditions compared. The number of quantified proteins and the number of comparisons are identical for both datasets. Could you explain to me where this difference in the adjusted p-values may come from, and is there any parameters in the groupComparison function that I could play with to minimize this effect, because I am loosing some meaningful protein candidates in the full dataset because of this slight increase of the adjusted p-values?

Thank you!

Best,

Dmytro

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: adjusted p-value calculation in msstats
parts:
Dear Dmytro,

I suggest that you compare two analyses step by step, to see where the differences arise. In principle, every step can be affected by adding one more run. In particular, very early in the process there are filters, such as 'remove features with too many missing values'. When an extra run is added these filters may keep more proteins, and a larger protein number affects the multiple testing correction (more proteins require more conservative decisions). I do not know how many replicates you have, but this will be particularly the case in studies with a small number of runs. This said, if the number of runs is small, I am surprised that adding a new run does not change the log2FC and the p-values. 

So in short, please compare the results at each step, starting from filtering and normalization. Hopefully it will help you clarify where exactly the difference occurs.

Thank you for using MSstats

Sincerely
Olga
